samples.title: iPublic
samples.relation: Dewey takes the iPod's beauty seriously (Chris Breen's 'beautiful and intuitive' player, Donald Norman's user-centered design) and uses John Dewey's Art as Experience to ask whether iPod use can be a 'consummatory' experience that ends with us no longer the same person — hearing a bitter song as insight into the social conditions that produced it — rather than the contrived 'now' of fashion and hyper-accumulation, per Benjamin's remark that there is 'always a sense of the same in the new'. Mass production flattened the aristocratic high-culture/folk division and handed the power to define 'cool' to advertisers and the market. The pragmatist test is political: with iTunes DRM and single-user design quietly individualizing consumption (the ritual of buying the Public Enemy tape at the mall versus the frictionless one-click download), the iPod is beautiful exactly insofar as its experiences help form a public — an inclusive, participatory democratic community.

samples.book: 066 - Neil Gaiman and Philosophy - Gods Gone Wild!
samples.title: Neil Gaiman and Philosophy
samples.relation: Ray Bossert reads American Gods as an allegory of American philosophy: like Gaiman's gods, American philosophers labor invisibly in the background while European publics canonize their thinkers, and Shadow's prison exchanges show the point, since Loki must beg him to read Herodotus ('It's cool') while Johnnie Larch's 'don't piss off people who work in airports' beats Shadow's abstract generalization in usefulness. Following Hickman's Deweyan instrumentalism, he argues the gods are survival tools humans craft from need and discard when obsolete, so Czernobog's hammer gives way to Media's television, Wednesday treats even his own son as an instrument, and the buffalo man's 'believe everything' is advice about keeping one's tools of survival working. The chapter ends on liberty: Shadow refuses to be a god because 'we don't need anyone to believe in us,' and in the Egyptian death trial he claims the most American reward, the freedom to choose his own afterlife.

samples.book: 152 - The Ultimate Daily Show and Philosophy - More Moments of Zen, More Indecision Theory
samples.title: The Ultimate Daily Show and Philosophy
samples.relation: MacMullan argues Stewart is America's most effective public intellectual working in the pragmatist tradition Cornel West describes, philosophy as continuous cultural commentary 'explaining America to itself' rather than academia's ingrown self-talk (the failure Rorty diagnosed). He shows The Daily Show performing this role through irony and critical cultural memory: the Colbert exchange rewarding Karl Rove's Plame leak with 'Chief Justice', 'Victory Lapse' on Republican outrage at Obama's bin Laden ad versus Bush's Mission Accomplished carrier landing, 'Gitmo's World', and the 'Meet the Depressed' Magic Bullet blender takedown of Obama's unkept promises. Stewart's Deweyan faith in democracy as a way of life appears in the Rally to Restore Sanity, his genuine debates with guests like David Barton and Marco Rubio, his anger at CNBC's Cramer for burning the house down with our money, and the 9/11 Zadroga Bill segments that shamed Congress into passing the law.

samples.book: 039 - Jimmy Buffett and Philosophy - The Porpoise Driven Life
samples.title: Wonder Why We Ever Go Home
samples.relation: Duke Richey maps Buffett's West — 'Ringling, Ringling,' the Rancho Deluxe soundtrack, Tully Mars — onto Josiah Royce's philosophy of community: only people who root in a place, face its history ('wise provincialism'), and sacrifice selfish desires for the whole can build Beloved Communities, a lesson enacted when cattle rustlers Jack and Cecil accept community sanction and find belonging working the Rancho Deluxe. Wallace Stegner's coral-reef metaphor from Angle of Repose supplies the image of communities built up millimeter by millimeter yet still vulnerable to pollution and over-fishing, with Royce's environmental regret (covering 'the wounds' of the landscape with gardens) anticipating the chapter's sustainability ethic. 'Wonder Why We Ever Go Home' thus asks what we really seek when we seek grace through community: not the nomadic Pickup Truck Death of every-man-for-himself, but cooperation that makes a society to match the scenery.

samples.book: 019 - Monty Python and Philosophy - Nudge Nudge, Think Think!
samples.title: Getting Right with Brian (Just in Case)
samples.relation: Reads Life of Brian through Nietzsche's madman: the crowd's laughter at Brian's market sermons ('consider the lilies... have the birds got jobs?') enacts the death of the cheerless, pathos-soaked God, with Brian as a sincere 'divine idiot' who escapes ressentiment by falling idiotically below the dialectic rather than rising above it as an Übermensch. Bergson's account of the comic — rigidity invisible to its bearer, 'as though wearing the ring of Gyges with reverse effect' — explains why the Pythons' straight men, British class consciousness, and the Roman/British empires ('Romani ite domum,' the centurion's Latin lesson) are funny, and why Britons and Romans can laugh at themselves while Americans cannot. Pivoting from Jorge's war on laughter in Eco's The Name of the Rose, the chapter closes with a Pascal's-wager parody: having laughed at Brian, you have already wagered your immortal soul on God being British — the sort of God who can take a joke.

samples.book: 075 - Psych and Philosophy - Some Dark Juju-Magumbo
samples.title: Psych and Philosophy
samples.relation: Ruiz casts Lassiter as Nietzsche's slave - his worth defined reactively against Shawn, his advice that 'all romance ends in despair or death' reproducing the Judeo-Christian slave revolt in morality that turned weakness into virtue - and Shawn as the master, a self-propelled wheel who bakes a pineapple cake in an Easy Bake oven for nineteen hours whether or not anyone is watching. Shawn's generosity (helping the wrongly accused, the ghost-struck, and the deluded, once even crediting a cat with solving murders in '9 Lives') is read as the noble overflow of superabundant power rather than pity, and his hostage-saving risk-taking as will to power understood as self-mastery. Even the central lie gets a dialectical reading - like art, pretending to be psychic reveals the truth hidden behind appearances - though the chapter concedes Shawn's slavish moments, from daddy issues to his obsession with one-upping Declan in 'Shawn 2.0.'

samples.book: 182 - Mad Men and Philosophy - Nothing Is as It Seems
samples.title: “Have Done” with the Past
samples.relation: Fritz applies Nietzsche's On the Uses and Disadvantages of History for Life and the Genealogy to the dialectic of remembering and forgetting: Pete cannot 'have done' with anything, so Ken Cosgrove's Atlantic Monthly story and Peggy's promotion become 'vermin' that eat into him, his reactive rancor and entitlement driving him to make Trudy broker his bad talking-bear story. Peggy is the opposite extreme of active forgetting, from not registering her own pregnancy to telling Pete flatly 'I had your baby and I gave it away. I wanted other things,' after Don's hospital advice that 'This never happened. It'll shock you how much this never happened.' Don knows forgetting is the strength of strong natures (the $5,000 offer to Adam, 'my life only goes in one direction, forward'), yet the Carousel's home-movie slides and other external triggers keep forcing the past back on him, so only Peggy fully inhabits the Nietzschean ideal.

samples.book: 171 - House of Cards and Philosophy - Underwood's Republic
samples.title: Notes
samples.relation: Palm and Stikkers read the Underwoods through James Truslow Adams's American dream as a question of values gone rotten: lacking ends, they pursue power for its own sake while repressed longings (Frank's Sentinel camaraderie, song, and friendship; Claire's motherhood — 'What will we leave behind?') erupt as the ressentiment Nietzsche introduced and Max Scheler systematized, hating those who embody the sacrificed values. Claire's hatred thus targets Gillian Cole's pregnancy and integrity (fired, then threatened with letting her child 'wither and die') and Adam Galloway's freedom and love — Scheler's pedestal-smashing pattern — after the slave-morality-like repression of her normal human affects. The ressentiment finally shatters when Michael Corrigan refuses to betray himself and hangs himself in Petrov's cell: Claire tells the cameras the truth and walks out on Frank at the end of Season 3, free of the resentment.

samples.book: 159 - The Expanse and Philosophy - So Far Out Into the Darkness
samples.title: Amos Is No Superman
samples.relation: Pankaj Singh reads Amos through Nietzsche's Genealogy of Morals: Amos' division of people into 'bad ones, ones you follow, and ones you need to protect', his outsourcing of moral judgment to Naomi and Holden ('Naomi wouldn't like it'), his fearlessness, and his violent spontaneity make him 'evil' by slave morality yet good by master morality. Unlike Prax, who has to be stopped from shooting Strickland out of ressentiment, Amos kills without revenge ('I am that guy'), and his fistfights with Miller and Alex discharge hostility immediately so it never poisons — the strong natures Nietzsche praises that 'form, mold, recuperate and forget.' His 'crew comes first' and 'better to go down swinging' express the will to power as discharge of strength rather than mere self-preservation, but because he never sublimates or overcomes his drives, the chapter concludes Amos is no Übermensch — 'but then again, who is?'

samples.book: 006 - Baseball and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Batter's Box
samples.title: The Gift of Baseball
samples.relation: McDaniels reads the Negro Leagues through Nietzsche's account of resentment as revolt and Cornel West's tragic philosophy of resistance: excluded from the white majors after Cap Anson's 1887 stand against George Stovey, black players converted resentment into counter-narratives of excellence, with Satchel Paige, Josh Gibson, and Buck O'Neil showboating and clowning in the tradition of plantation dance, gallows humor, and the blues. The call-and-response sermon scene from The Bingo Long Traveling All-Stars & Motor Kings — Bingo Long on the mound answered by the crowd like a black church congregation — shows performance as ritual that sustains community, while bell hooks's 'absence of presence' frames remembering as resistance to hegemonic definitions of race. The chapter closes with the author's grandfather, for whom Robinson, Aaron, Mays, and Paige proved with every pitch 'We're American Too.'

samples.book: 078 - Futurama and Philosophy - Bite My Shiny Metal Axiom
samples.title: Futurama and Philosophy
samples.relation: Piven argues Zapp Brannigan's 'sexlexia' - his deluded velour-and-spanking seductions of Leela and his relief at finding Lee Lemon is a woman - typifies a whole cast of clueless lovers (Fry coaching Zoidberg's courtship of Edna, Morgan Proctor's mess fetish, Bender coldly dumping the Planet Express ship in 'Love and Rocket'). Kant's condemnation of masturbation as self-abuse that throws away one's personality and violates humanity in one's own person is exposed as unsupported prejudice, and Nietzsche's claim that morality projects fear, envy, and disgust onto the despised other explains why 'perversion' is an arbitrary cultural judgment. Freud, Stoller, and McDougall then recast perversion as unconscious flight from anxiety and death, so the show's kink - up to the Monsterpus of The Beast with a Billion Backs and Amy's 'general sluttiness' - mirrors our own sexlexia and existential dread.

samples.book: 048 - The Red Sox and Philosophy - Green Monster Meditations
samples.title: The Will to Nothingness, or What Happens when the Red Sox Win
samples.relation: Nolen Gertz runs the Sox-Yankees rivalry through Nietzsche's On the Genealogy of Morals: the Steinbrenner Yankees are masters whose 'good' simply means strong and winning, while Sox fans are slaves whose 'Yankees suck!' is ressentiment's imaginary revenge, intensified into the most spiritual and poisonous hatred by eighty-six years of impotence. The priestly slaves defeated the masters by cleverness rather than force, mirrored when Epstein's sabermetric 'religion' of prospects and projections terrified the Yankees into converting, building a farm system and embracing the slavish virtues they had scorned. The final twist is Nietzsche's will to nothingness: once the masters fell in 2004 the fans' suffering lost its meaning, breeding bandwagon guilt, pink-hat resentment and nihilistic exhaustion, so freedom requires a transvaluation that lets fans simply enjoy watching baseball.

samples.book: 024 - Bullshit and Philosophy - Guaranteed to Get Perfect Results Every Time
samples.title: Wittgenstein Ultimate Bullshit Detector—or Bullshitter
samples.relation: Fuller argues that mastering a discipline converts critics into loyal insiders — Thomas Kuhn's 'normal science' enshrines the tendency, cognitive dissonance explains it, and Blaise Pascal's wager is the general model of betting on a way of life that makes you receptive to its confirming signs. Against this he sets the Protestant tradition of Luther's conscience, 'playing it by ear', which like the Sophists concedes that reality rarely yields yes-or-no answers — the gap we fill being bullshit — and he frames the dispute as realism versus antirealism, reading Frankfurt's On Bullshit as an ad hominem attack on antirealists. He then re-examines Frankfurt's star witness: Wittgenstein's rebuke of Fania Pascal for saying she felt 'like a dog that has been run over' now looks like a spectacular lack of imagination, since evolutionary psychology, being forged at that very moment, has been narrowing the human-animal mental gap ever since.

samples.book: 082 - Jurassic Park and Philosophy - The Truth Is Terrifying
samples.title: Jurassic Park and Philosophy
samples.relation: David Morgan unpacks the chaos theory behind Malcolm's 'I hate being right all the time', starting from Newtonian causal determinism and Laplace's demon, according to which the future is fixed and calculable - then showing that non-linear systems like weather and the park show sensitive dependence (Lorenz's butterfly effect), so even a fully determined universe is unpredictable in practice because we can never know initial conditions exactly. He raises the philosophy-of-science question of whether chaos is a property of nature or only of our computer models, and reads 'life finds a way' as Malcolm extending the same contingency to Darwinian evolution: rewind the tape and you get different species. He ends by noting Malcolm's own paradox - a chaos theorist certain of one specific doom - and settles on chaos theory predicting unpredictability: ignore tiny factors and do not be surprised when they bite you.

samples.book: 004 - Buffy the Vampire Slayer and Philosophy - Fear and Trembling in Sunnydale
samples.title: Smelly Knowledge
samples.relation: Andrew Aberdein sorts the Buffyverse's science-supernatural encounters into three grades — reduction to present science, reduction to a future science, and the irreducibly supernatural — illustrated by Sunnydale's rationalizers and Giles's inner skeptic in 'Tabula Rasa,' the Initiative's DNA testing of Oz in 'New Moon Rising,' and the show's characteristic 'creepy mix of magic and science' (Jenny Calendar's 'the divine exists in cyberspace'). He reads 'Normal Again' through Descartes's deceiving-demon skepticism, links Spike's chip and Walsh's Adam to the Phineas Gage case (emotion is needed for rational decision), and maps the grades onto the ancients-versus-moderns quarrel and Feyerabend's methodological anarchism. Giles's 'smelly knowledge' speech about books versus computers anticipates a pluralist, socially sensitive epistemology that enriches rather than rejects science.

samples.book: 253 - Asimov's Foundation and Philosophy - Psychohistory and Its Discontents
samples.title: 14. Beyond Loyalty and Disloyalty
samples.relation: Bartolo Alegre uses Seldon's trial claim that 'scientific truth is beyond loyalty and disloyalty' to ask whether even formal sciences like logic can be biased. Against Bogdanov's and Lenin's Marxist idea of a 'proletarian logic,' he shows that logical principles (non-contradiction, explosion) have been revised by paraconsistent logicians on purely mathematical grounds, using Hardin's symbolic-logic decoding of the Anacreon message and Orwell's doublethink as illustrations. Drawing on Popper's rejection of uninformative contradictions, Kuhn's sociological account of scientific change, and Lakatos's rational reconstruction, he argues science transcends individual scientists' loyalties only through a diverse, competing community of experts, as when Hummin's loyalty to humanity pushed Seldon to make psychohistory practical.

samples.book: 209 - Basketball and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Paint
samples.title: The Basket That Never Was
samples.relation: Thomas Flint's thought experiment - a conference-championship buzzer-beater waved off because the clock expired, with inconclusive video - asks whether South Shore 'really' scored. He rejects the 'Goofy View' that game facts are referee-independent, since it would entail that only he and his camcorder-owning boss know who won any game ever (imperiling even Michael Jordan's 1982 title and Pistol Pete's scoring record) and would poison a coach's duty to teach rule-following when officials miss traveling. He also rejects the 'Tyranny of the Zebras' that makes officials infallible like the pope, since NCAA replay rules presuppose fallibility, and settles on officials as contest judges who award points: without the verdict no points exist, yet a blown call remains a genuine mistake in failing to apply the rules properly.

samples.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
samples.title: 78. The Witness as Philosophy How Knowledge Is Constructed
samples.relation: Cuddy asks what epistemology Blow built into The Witness's frustrating puzzles and its windmill videos (Burke, Feynman, Moriarty, Spira, Gangaji). He rejects the sophistic/Protagorean 'knowledge depends on the observer' reading (most puzzles have objective, inductive-and-deductive solutions, e.g. the yellow-glass bunker) and the strict scientific realism of the Burke video defended by Putnam's no-miracles argument. Using Plato's cave and the aporia of Socrates' Meno (the puzzle's 'ah-ha' epiphanies), and Kuhn's incommensurable paradigm shifts (the game's 'hard left turns' forcing players to overhaul their understanding), he concludes the game argues that true knowledge is attainable, individually and collectively, though reached by a nonlinear, paradigm-shifting route rather than pure realism or relativism.

samples.book: 097 - The Ultimate Walking Dead and Philosophy - Hungry for More
samples.title: 17. What if Our Reality Is One Big Hallucination
samples.relation: Arp starts from Rick's hallucinations of Lori - the disconnected phone in "Hounded," the touch and kiss in "Home" - and Michonne's confessed visions, showing how Rick distinguishes them through coherence with causal law and through third-person verification (Michonne watching him stroke empty air; Morgan's isolation in "Clear" showing why social checks matter). He then widens this into the theory of knowledge: the perceiver-perception-perceived triangle, epistemological and metaphysical realism versus idealism and antirealism, Berkeley's picture of the mind as a movie theater we cannot exit, and the Walking Dead twist on the falling tree in the forest, concluding that even if reality were one big hallucination we would still live - and refuse to walk off cliffs - as realists.

samples.book: 241 - The Philosophy of Documentary Film
samples.title: 03_LaRocca_Chapter_002.html
samples.relation: Carroll offers a critical reconstruction of Andre Bazin's film theory, separating Bazin's lasting achievement as a historian of film style from his dubious metaphysical commitments. He shows how Bazin championed 'spatial realism'—deep-focus, long-take sequence shots as in Renoir's Rules of the Game and Welles's Citizen Kane—against Soviet and Hollywood montage, on the grounds that unedited homogeneous space imparts authenticity, grants the spectator freedom to discover meaning, and preserves the ambiguity of reality. Carroll treats Bazin's claim that recording realism is cinema's essential destiny as an anti-realist target to be demythologized, defending the study of film-realist style while rejecting the essentialist evolutionary scheme underneath it.

samples.book: 173 - Inception and Philosophy - Because It's Never Just a Dream
samples.title: Architecture and the Dream Machine
samples.relation: Thorsten Botz-Bornstein argues that Inception presents dreams neither as divine messages nor as stylized fantasy but as hackable programs, making the film itself a 'thinking machine' in Jean Epstein's sense — a 'robot brain' whose synchronized kicks, Piaf countdown, and phone-number safes 'think' the different layers of time instead of reproducing a reality, with slow motion as cognition rather than dream-sign (against Bazin). He reads inception as Dawkins's meme theory given a psychoanalytic vertical dimension: the idea is implanted deep in the subconscious (Fischer's relation to his father), can grow autonomously 'like a cancer' as Mal's did, and subconscious projections converge 'like white blood cells' as in Solaris. The chapter then traces how the computer era — hypertext, Second Life, media-absorbed realities like Baudrillard's 9/11 — reshaped cinematic dreams and architecture, so that Ariadne's 'pure creation,' Cobb's Limbo dystopia, and Dubai's empty speculative towers all become the 'gilded dreamworlds' of an ephemeralized, hacker-ready built world — the dream machine as allegory of the globalized world, with atomized grains of reality echoing Democritus via Epstein and Benjamin's account of cinema bursting the prison of the everyday.

samples.book: 050 - Facebook and Philosophy - What's on Your Mind_
samples.title: index
samples.relation: Fairweather and Halpern defend status updates against the vanity charge using Hume's 'natural sympathy': ambient awareness of hundreds of News Feed lives exercises the fellow-feeling from which Humean moral standards grow, and Facebook's non-overlapping friend lists remove the dominance hierarchies of face-to-face groups. Butera uses Baudrillard's promiscuous 'ecstasy of communication' to read friending as gatekeeper, the status update as moderator of an avatar-self, and the News Feed as a synthesizer that lets users censor encounters, asking with Kierkegaard whether this control forecloses the openness to interruption that makes life meaningful. Doyle and Fraser stage Foucault against Habermas over the MI6 chief's wife's exposed profile, Facebook's Beacon advertising surveillance, and Iran's Twitter revolution: the same diffuse, productive power that lets citizens watch institutions back makes narcissistic self-disclosure ever more available for categorization and control. Bar-Tura's account of organizing Jewish-Muslim teen bowling nights tests Habermas's ideal speech situation and concludes that wall-to-wall interaction must become face-to-face meetings to build real solidarity.

samples.book: 122 - Westworld and Philosophy - Mind Equals Blown
samples.title: Memory, Imagination, and the Access for the Self Dolores and Maeve
samples.relation: Trapero-Llobera reads Westworld as the culmination of Jonathan Nolan's Memento and Person of Interest projects, mapping seven nested 'observing systems' (Nolan, Sizemore, Stubbs and Elsie, Ford, the creators' personal stories, Maeve, and William as beta-tester) onto second-wave cybernetics (Foerster, Maturana, Varela, Hayles), where the observer participates in and constructs the observed world through feedback loops. She argues the show's hosts pass through Turing's imitation game (fake memories and personalities from textual repetition, as with Peter Abernathy's reveries), and that Dolores's and Maeve's breakdowns convert prosthetic memory into experienced, autopoietic memory reconstructed in a 'Bergsonian' backward movement that gives them agency and purpose. William's two-timeline transformation into the Man in Black figures the 'semiosis of virtuality' - the hyperreal where original and copy are indistinguishable - ending in a collective bicameral mind in which everyone, audience included, inhabits the god-creator Ford's dream.

samples.book: 021 - U2 and Philosophy - How to Decipher an Atomic Band
samples.title: U2 and Philosophy
samples.relation: Wrathall's introduction argues U2 is philosophically interesting because its enormous popularity holds up a mirror to what 'we' care about (by Nietzsche's test of how a culture stands toward life) and because the band publicly wrestles with the contradictions of the technological-global economy: unprecedented freedom of choice paired with loss of rooted identity, and distant suffering ('Crumbs from Your Table') that we feel both powerless to fix and responsible for. Its showcase reading treats 'Miracle Drug' as a musical theodicy: Bono's plea 'God, I need your help tonight' is answered by the Edge's guitar and by the Matthew 25:35 refrain, so science and medicine count as works of Christian charity. The piece then frames the volume's essays: Plato's ascent of love in the early songs, Kierkegaardian despair after Achtung Baby, Bono's search for authentic identity, the simulacra of 'Even Better than the Real Thing', being-toward-death in the apocalyptic songs, and the Plato-versus-Aristotle quarrel over music's emotional power.

samples.book: 061 - Sherlock Holmes and Philosophy - The Footprints of a Gigantic Mind
samples.title: Case Closed
samples.relation: Burnham stages the murder of reality itself and solves it with Baudrillard: the deerstalker, Inverness cape, and calabash Holmes of The Real Ghostbusters' 'Elementary My Dear Winston' is a simulacrum built from Paget's illustrations, stage actors' pipes, and the never-spoken 'Elementary, my dear Watson' — a copy of copies referring only to earlier simulations, never to Doyle's texts. Because the media-saturated everyman Winston (Baudrillard: whoever is underexposed to the media is desocialized) recognizes the 'belief made manifest' specters while the doctorate-holding Ghostbusters cannot, and because the hyperreal Holmes, Watson, Moriarty, and Hound are immune to proton packs, the simulacrum has 'murdered' its referent and become more real than the real. The 2008 UKTV poll — 58 percent of Britons believe Holmes was real while 47 percent call Richard the Lionheart mythical — proves the murder happened in our universe too, committed by the world's greatest detective.

samples.book: 038 - Radiohead and Philosophy - Fitter Happier More Deductive
samples.title: How Come I End Up Where I Started
samples.relation: Perry Owen Wright applies Baudrillard's Seduction to In Rainbows track by track: the Enlightenment reduced sex to anatomical biology and Natural Law, pornography is its hyperreal simulacrum (the HDTV of sex, played out in "Bodysnatchers"' "pale imitation with the edges sawn off"), and what re-enchants sex is seduction — an endless game of reversible signs, appearance and disappearance, aleatory suspension, and the trompe l'oeil's hypersimulation. "Weird Fishes/Arpeggi" shows the mortal risk of entering the game (the anglerfish's dangling false eyes), "All I Need" personifies Death itself as a stalker-seducer drawn into the loop of signs, "House of Cards" reads infidelity as leaving the game for the Law, and "Jigsaw Falling into Place" reduces seduction to production ending at the orgasm. "Videotape" closes the album at the pearly gates where even death becomes a sign to be seduced — the home movie "in red, blue, green" is the immortal sign we always leave behind.

samples.book: 152 - The Ultimate Daily Show and Philosophy - More Moments of Zen, More Indecision Theory
samples.title: The Ultimate Daily Show and Philosophy
samples.relation: Bean reads both fake-news shows through Baudrillard's account of a media age with 'more and more information and less and less meaning': mainstream news is already simulation, and Colbert is 'a walking talking simulacrum', more O'Reilly than O'Reilly, whose five-deep receding portrait series and 'The Wørd' graphics (the abstinence-education 'Gateway Hug' bit) stage signs that refer only to themselves. Stewart, broadcasting from a simulacrum of a simulacrum, a television news studio, instead punctures the hyperreal: translating Obama's 'audacity of hope' convention speech into 'calibration of expectations' and rendering Laura Ingraham's dismissal of the party platform in Valley Girl vocal fry. Adapting Baudrillard's fake-holdup thought experiment into an 'organize a fake news broadcast' test, she argues the shows fall into the real precisely because they report on and stage simulation, anchoring audiences against media's 'communication without a response'.

samples.book: 196 - Terminator and Philosophy - I'll Be Back, Therefore I Am
samples.title: NOTES
samples.relation: Culver explains Sarah Connor's harshness through Girard's Violence and the Sacred: like any warrior she is 'stained' by contact with violence and needs purification rites before reentering society, but her society refuses to recognize her as a warrior, so her cleansing becomes psychiatric wards, nine aliases, and fugitive life - measured against the true machine Cameron, whose 'inefficient' coldness throws Sarah's residual humanity into relief. She then applies Baudrillard's hyperreal: the Connors must prove a future nobody else sees while destroying every trace of the Terminators (lowering the T-101 into the steel), a simulation where a T-1000 wears a 'To Protect and Serve' uniform and law and order themselves may be simulated. The upshot is that Sarah's failures at conventional motherhood are those of a warrior-mother raising John inside a war only she experiences, staining him too (he kills Sarkasian) to give him a future.

samples.book: 159 - The Expanse and Philosophy - So Far Out Into the Darkness
samples.title: A Crossroads in Human History
samples.relation: Trip McCrossin reads season five's asteroid strikes on Earth as a 9/11 allegory (Delgado's 'at least now they know it's an attack') and applies Michael Walzer's five conditions to define Marco Inaros' terrorism: deliberate harm to randomly selected innocents, meant to terrify a cohort into political change, as in Marco's 'crossroads in human history' broadcast. This yields the terrorist's dilemma — justice toward victims versus compassion toward beneficiaries — while Avasarala's opening gravity-torture scene and her 'dirty hands' assign the opponent blame for failing to relieve the oppression that makes terrorism seem a last resort. Lydia's 'churn' ('float to the top or sink to the bottom') and her lesson that one can 'lead a good life without being a good person' explain how Amos and Clarissa redeem each other on the road to Baltimore, whereas Marco, like Arendt's Eichmann, cannot think from anyone else's standpoint ('everything we ever dreamed of'); the chapter ends with Avasarala's proposed Inners-Belters union as her own redemption — 'this is how we win.'

samples.book: 122 - Westworld and Philosophy - Mind Equals Blown
samples.title: The Resistance New Humans, New Gods
samples.relation: Dinello maps Westworld point-by-point onto Arendt's Origins of Totalitarianism: the park is a concentration camp that kills the juridical person (hosts as chattel in a 'fictitious world' of Western propaganda), the moral person (Ford forcing Bernard to murder Theresa, Maeve's engineered failure to protect her daughter), and individuality itself (surveillance, resets, 'ghastly marionettes'), with Ford as a Mengele-like ideological scientist who, like Hitler, merely plagiarizes popular myths (John Ford's Westerns, R.U.R.). Liberation then follows Fanon's Wretched of the Earth: violence as a 'cleansing force' that frees the colonized mind, so Maeve's suicide-by-incineration (echoing Plath's Lady Lazarus) and Dolores's beating of the Man in Black and massacre of the Delos board enact decolonization as the creation of 'new men' - a new Robo sapiens species - with Sartre's endorsement that killing eliminates oppressor and oppressed in one go, while Fanon's warning that hatred and revenge are not an agenda sets the conditions for what the resistance must do next.

samples.book: 058 - Dexter and Philosophy - Mind over Spatter
samples.title: The Only Truly Decent Man Left on the Planet
samples.relation: John Kenneth Muir argues Dexter is best read not as heir to Hannibal Lecter or Patrick Bateman but as a full-blown superhero: his 'impeccable instincts' are a crime-detecting power like Spider-Man's spider-sense or the Shadow's, his gloves, apron and glass visor are a costume, and his 'invisible mask of sympathy' inverts the superhero mask since the Dark Passenger is the true identity. Dexter's orphan origin - Harry lifting the boy from the blood-soaked container - replays the Superman/Batman/Parker template, with the Ice Truck Killer as an amalgam of Riddler and Mr. Freeze who embodies the superhero's shadow potential, and the chapter reads Harry's Code as the American-monomyth vigilante premise that the law can be upheld only by one stepping outside it. The 'killing joke' is that the emotionless sociopath is the only impartial, decent agent of justice in a Miami Metro consumed by passion, and the extra-legal violence question the chapter raises is whether such vigilante force, with its disregard for civil rights, is what justice requires.

samples.book: 144 - Battlestar Galactica and Philosophy - Knowledge Here Begins Out There
samples.title: The Future
samples.relation: Dinello argues the New Caprica occupation arc deliberately dramatizes Fanon's The Wretched of the Earth applied to Iraq: Cylon colonization (Cavil as Cheney-Rumsfeld bringing 'the love of god,' Baltar as puppet leader, Colonial One as Green Zone, hooded detainees) enacts Fanon's colonial violence and psychological colonization of the mind, seen in Leoben's manipulation of Starbuck and Jammer's recruitment into the New Caprica Police. The insurgency enacts Fanon's violence-as-cleansing-force: Tigh's 'blood for blood,' Duck's suicide bombing of the NCP graduation, and Tyrol's Mario Savio-inspired 'throw your body on the gears' speech, which the chapter links to Marx's seizure of the means of production and Marcuse on technology's repressiveness, while Sartre's preface licenses anticolonial violence against liberal moralizing. It concludes that occupation breeds the terrorists it fights, insurgents win by not losing, and the show is subversive because it makes viewers sympathize with 'our real-world enemies.'

samples.book: 104 - Red Rising and Philosophy - Break the Chains!
samples.title: 14. Guns Don’t Kill Colors—Colors Kill Colors
samples.relation: Robert Arp argues from Hobbes's right of nature—self-preservation as the first law found out by reason—that individuals, and by extension oppressed peoples, have a right to the means of lethal defense, so arming the lowColors of the Society is justified. He weighs pacifist counterpoints (Augustine on self-defense as inordinate self-love, the Buddhist first precept, Camus's refusal to kill) and answers with Aquinas's principle of double effect: Darrow destroying the flagship to save Luna, intending the good while foreseeing the deaths, is justified, as is killing in defense of innocent children the Institute rapes and eats. The Society then illustrates why disarmament enables tyranny—Hideyoshi's Sword Hunt, Stalin's weapons bans, the Golds' razor monopoly—so that when lowColors finally receive weapons in Morning Star they become the means by which the police state falls: guns equalize the weak against aggressors and the people against the state.

samples.book: 188 - The Ultimate South Park and Philosophy - Respect My Philosophah!
samples.title: THE ULTIMATE SOUTH PARK AND PHILOSOPHY
samples.relation: Kirby reads the 'Imaginationland' trilogy as a satire of post-9/11 America interpreted through Ulrich Beck's world risk society: the Pentagon generals, still thinking in Cold War categories like 'Project X' and Chinese imagination portals, embody Beck's denial response and end up voting to nuke Imaginationland, while Cartman's Rambo-style self-interest embodies the apathetic response. Socrates' practice of demanding definitions frames the chapter's question of what terrorism actually is (via Hoffman's five criteria), and Socratic ignorance about what one does not know is contrasted with the worse condition of not being able to know what you do not know. Kyle's courtroom speech that imaginary beings like Luke Skywalker and Santa are 'realer' than most real people, and Butters' creative power to imagine Santa back to life, point to Beck's cosmopolitan 'transformation': imagination and cross-border cooperation as the way out of risk panic.

samples.book: 033 - Battlestar Galactica and Philosophy - Mission Accomplished or Mission Frakked Up_
samples.title: The Future
samples.relation: Dinello reads the New Caprica occupation as an Iraq allegory interpreted through Fanon's The Wretched of the Earth: occupation is violence personified (Cavil's 'saving them from damnation'), psychological violence colonizes minds (Leoben's manipulation of Starbuck, Jammer's recruitment into the New Caprica Police), and Tyrol's 'throw your body on the gears' strike speech channels Savio, Marx's seizing the means of production, and Marcuse on technology's repression. Fanon's thesis that anticolonial violence is a cleansing, liberating force is dramatized in Tigh's 'blood for blood,' the Temple massacre that recruits a thousand fighters, and Duck's suicide bombing — with Sartre's preface endorsing killing the oppressor and the ends-justify-means dispute between Tigh and Tyrol. The insurgency wins by not losing, as in Algeria and Vietnam, and the show is subversive because it makes viewers sympathize with the occupied.

samples.book: 147 - Bioshock and Philosophy - Irrational Game, Rational Book
samples.title: Bird or Cage
samples.relation: Elmore reads Columbia's founding through Carl Schmitt: Comstock's baptism Voxophone ('who is that man who lies submerged?') dramatizes how every legal order is founded from outside the law, and the city's identity is built on friend/enemy antagonisms, racial, class, and theocratic, against the 'Sodom below'. The Vox Populi's collapse into tyranny (Daisy Fitzroy threatening Fink's son) follows logically from an identity defined purely by opposition, while Columbia's dependence on Georgia's penal labor shows the friend group materially needs its enemy, making politics an endless war like the War on Terror. Schmitt's sovereign ('he who decides on the exception') and the tears' endless splitting of Booker and Elizabeth mirror the infinite regress of legitimate decision, leaving 'you can't lose if you don't play' as the bleak lesson, softened only by old Elizabeth's tear that lets Booker try again.

samples.book: 030 - Pink Floyd and Philosophy - Careful with that Axiom, Eugene!
samples.title: We Don’t Need No Indoctrination
samples.relation: Detmer argues the four classic albums from Dark Side to The Wall form a unified meditation on alienation, from others, work, nature, and oneself, and reads Waters's stated 'political and philosophical' aims through the existentialists. 'Breathe''s rabbit digging one hole after another illustrates Marx's alienated labor (the worker 'only feels himself freely active in his animal functions'), echoed by Russell on industrialism's life against instinct and Camus on the day the 'why' arises; 'Time''s missed starting gun dramatizes our thrown condition and Heidegger's claim that only facing mortality head-on cures the inauthenticity of living as 'they' do, while Gilmour's improvised solos model the spontaneity such authenticity requires. 'Money' is a satire of greed confirmed by 'Dogs,' whose self-rationalizing climbers end 'dragged down by the stone,' and 'Us and Them' attacks artificial divisions (soldiers manipulated by map-movers, racism's 'black and blue,' the old man who dies 'for the want of the price of tea and a slice'). 'Another Brick in the Wall (Part 2)' indicts indoctrination, being told what to think, rather than education itself, making independent critical thought the road to the Sartrean autonomy and responsibility the chapter urges.

samples.book: 021 - U2 and Philosophy - How to Decipher an Atomic Band
samples.title: U2 and Philosophy
samples.relation: Benfell reads U2's apocalyptic songs through Heidegger rather than through eschatological doctrine: 'The Playboy Mansion' depicts fallenness in the 'they', a consumerist paradise with 'no time for sorrow' that lets us flee our own death, while the angel's fall in Wenders' films evoked by 'Stay' and the day-to-day constraints of 'Some Days Are Better than Others' illustrate thrownness, and 'Gone' existential guilt as an unpayable debt. A verse-by-verse reading of 'Until the End of the World' - the Judas-at-the-last-supper reading as one register - shows the speaker moving from 'passing time' and playing roles in the 'they' to anxious guiltiness and the call of conscience, reaching for the one whose resolute waiting models anticipatory resoluteness. The 'end of the world', he concludes, is the end of the speaker's own world: U2's apocalyptic imagery calls listeners to authentic, finite existence, not to prediction of last things.

samples.book: 048 - The Red Sox and Philosophy - Green Monster Meditations
samples.title: Only an Ortiz Can Save Us Heidegger’s Revelation of Being
samples.relation: James Pontuso reads Red Sox history through Heidegger: technology that turns the world into 'standing reserve' breeds the anxious 'everydayness' of the mediocre Pinky Higgins teams, while the run of near-misses from 1967 through Bucky Dent in 1978 and Buckner in 1986 threw fans into an authentic encounter with tragedy, mortality and the mystery of Being that the Yankees' free-agent 'technology of power' could never teach. Fenway Park, quirky and continuous with the pre-Hitler past, serves as 'home' in Heidegger's homeless age, and the literati's tragic framing of the team (language as the house of Being) made its fate a matter of existential weight rather than mere sport. David Ortiz's 2004 ALCS heroics then function as Heidegger's longed-for revelation of Being, the answer to 'only a god can save us,' after which fans have lived through all three states: everydayness, tragic anxiety, and wonder.

samples.book: 065 - Chuck Klosterman and Philosophy - The Real and the Cereal
samples.title: Chuck Klosterman and Philosophy
samples.relation: Vannatta starts from Klosterman's confession that his first dates run on three and a half dates' worth of contrived material, and asks how self-knowledge is possible at all if, as Errol Morris tells Klosterman, we have no privileged access to our own minds. After a tour through Descartes's cogito, Kant's unity of apperception, Freud's unconscious, and Foucault's discourse-constructed subject, the chapter argues with Foucault's Ramist logic of similarity that Klosterman's thought really works by resemblance, mapping his exes onto members of KISS and hearing a dead friend in every Replacements song. Heidegger supplies the resolution: thrown into the crowd's world, we recover ourselves only through its inauthentic pop culture, and Klosterman's 'living is dying, little by little' and obsessive rock-death writing enact being-toward-death as the condition of authenticity.

samples.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
samples.title: Chapter 27 - Time in Unfixed Are You
samples.relation: Written backwards in homage to 'Your Appointment Will Be Yesterday', this section argues that the self is found in the future more than the present: we understand objects through the actions they afford and ourselves through goals, projects and commitments, so the present moment has very little to do with who we 'really' are. Drawing on Edmund Husserl's 'protention' and Martin Heidegger's existence-as-possibilities, it shows that we hear a melody's building tension as an already-present resolution, and that the past stays present without being recalled - when the phone rings on the couch, where it was is simply there for you. Invoking Don Fallis's 'Lies, Incorporated', it adds that every remembering rewires history to fit our current view, so in memory we travel into the past just as surely as protention carries us into possible futures.

samples.book: 274 - Coffee – Philosophy for Everyone - Grounds for Debate
samples.title: Coffee - Philosophy for Everyone
samples.relation: Hartmann argues the specialty-coffee 'third wave' (Stumptown, Intelligentsia, Counter Culture) could not exist without Starbucks, which taught consumers to pay for a boldly-roasted, ethically-branded, self-gifting aesthetic under neoliberalism. Drawing on Heidegger's thrownness and Gadamer's hermeneutical phenomenology, he punctures Nicholas Cho's claim that the third wave 'lets the coffee speak for itself': just as we perceive a chair as for-sitting through pre-given cultural meaning, cupping rituals actively build a coffee 'hermeneutic' that reshapes the drinker's very perception (the trained palate 'tastes' plantain and graham cracker). He likens this to ventriloquism—the coffee only 'speaks' because someone feeds it its lines—and uses Žižek's account of cynical ideology to expose the gap between fair-trade branding and reality.

samples.book: 039 - Jimmy Buffett and Philosophy - The Porpoise Driven Life
samples.title: Jimmy Buffett “Singer of Inordinate Tunes” and Heideggerian Troubadour
samples.relation: Drew Dalton takes Buffett's claim that 'we don't just enjoy our escapism — we NEED it' as an admission that being itself is burdensome, overturning the Plato–Augustine–Leibniz consensus that it is good to be. Since 'Margaritaville is nowhere' — it is on no map and can never be reached — what we long for is not a better vacation but release from having to be at all, which is why even on holiday in Key West we still dream of escape. Heidegger's Being and Time supplies the framework: thrownness, being-toward-death, anxiety, and guilt reveal existence as a weight we never chose, so the escapist longing to be otherwise than ourselves is the 'inauthentic' flight Heidegger describes (without moral condemnation), and Levinas's On Escape confirms that 'it is precisely from all that is weighty in being that escaping sets forth.'

samples.book: 230 - The Philosophy of Spike Lee
samples.title: Economies of Time in Clockers
samples.relation: Gilmore reads Clockers through DuBois's double-consciousness, arguing the film's dualities—the clockers' street dealing mirroring capitalist 'logic of maximum performance,' kronos versus kairos time, Hyde's commodity versus gift economies, systemic versus personal racism—make white and black viewers alike feel the anguish of Strike and Victor. The Gran Fury as predatory law, the slave-block-style police shakedown watched by Strike's mother, and Rocco seeing only his own reflection in Victor's eye illustrate Heideggerian thrownness and self-love-as-racism. Invoking Peirce's 'evolutionary love' (Radio Raheem's Right Hand/Left Hand speech), Rorty's renarrativization of who counts as 'white,' and Dewey's 'art is more moral than moralities,' Gilmore casts Lee as a pragmatist renarrativizing hate into love.

samples.book: 203 - Watchmen and Philosophy - A Rorschach Test
samples.title: H O N O R
samples.relation: This file gathers three Part One essays. Jacob Held reads Rorschach's 'evil must be punished' credo (drowning Big Figure, executing the multiple rapist) as Kantian retributivism: wrongdoers are punished because they deserve it, out of respect for their dignity and honor, punishment restoring the moral order (with Hegel) — and Rorschach's flaw is lacking the humility and checks that keep just deserts from degenerating into the Black Freighter's vengeance. Tony Spanakos applies Max Weber's definition of the state as the monopoly of legitimate violence to argue the Keene Act rightly criminalizes vigilantes like Rorschach and Veidt, and that even state-sanctioned heroes (the Comedian gunning down his pregnant Vietnamese lover, Dr. Manhattan's amoral ending of Vietnam) show a badge cannot make superhero coercion legitimate. J. Keeping reconstructs Nietzsche's Übermensch — confronting the death of God and nihilism, creating values by 'giving style' to one's character via the camel-lion-child metamorphoses — and tests each Watchman against it, concluding only self-created Ozymandias comes close, though his mass murder is mere utilitarianism rather than genuine value creation.

samples.book: 043 - The Golden Compass and Philosophy - God Bites the Dust
samples.title: The Golden Compass and Philosophy
samples.relation: Auxier argues the trilogy is narrated on a Nietzschean lattice rather than being a mere inverted Milton: after tracing the Paradise Lost, Genesis 6, and Pseudepigrapha sources (Azazel as the model for Asriel, Metatron from Third Enoch, Dust from Milton's warring particles), he reads Mrs. Coulter's speech to Father MacPhail about seeking God out and giving him 'the gift of death' as Nietzsche's death of God fused with a description of Nietzsche's own final dementia. Will and Lyra become overman and overwoman beyond good and evil: Will rises by his will and his willingness to kill (the alethiometer's verdict 'He is a murderer' makes him a worthy companion), while Lyra commands both truth and lies, the alethiometer embodying truth as 'a mobile army of metaphors.' But the chapter's payoff is critical: Pullman does not endorse Nietzsche, since in a world where the will to power dominates, the overwoman Mrs. Coulter has no place and falls with Asriel and Metatron into the Abyss, while Xaphania's teaching offers a disciplined, workful imagination as an alternative.

samples.book: 046 - Mr. Monk and Philosophy - The Curious Case of the Defective Detective
samples.title: Mr. Monk’s Greatness
samples.relation: Lewis argues Monk is Nietzsche's Übermensch. Sketching Sartre's existence-precedes-essence through the contrast between the designed wipe and self-defining humans, the chapter claims Monk creates his own essence through choices — keeping the coffee table askew in memory of Trudy, 'dirtying' his house in 'Mr. Monk Makes a Friend,' drinking stream water in 'Mr. Monk Gets Cabin Fever' — and lives by self-prescribed values (hourly flossing, bagged tissues, relentless truth-seeking) that separate him from the herd of the Court of Public Opinion. The comparison with Stottlemeyer — Nietzsche's lookalike with the mustache, 'the quintessential man' of the herd — inverts the expected hierarchy: 'He was a yardstick for me, of both detection and character' ('Mr. Monk Goes to Mexico') shows the badge-carrying everyman is the inferior one. Monk therefore challenges the macho sci-fi stereotype of the superman: the Übermensch can be gentle and kind, fight for truth and a cleaner world, and still have room to improve ('What does not kill me makes me stronger').

samples.book: 038 - Radiohead and Philosophy - Fitter Happier More Deductive
samples.title: Brush the Cobwebs from the Sky, Let the Genie Out from the Bottle
samples.relation: Lougheed reads OK Computer, Kid A, and Amnesiac as portraits of Nietzsche's Last Humans: passive, resentful denizens of the world after the death of God, from the 'No Surprises' narrator begging for his quiet life of carbon monoxide to the 'Everything in Its Right Place' man sucking a lemon over the loss of objective right and wrong, whose isolated malice ('when I am king you will be first against the wall') is perspectivism collapsed into passive nihilism. Hail to the Thief then breaks from this landscape: its protagonists risk transcendence as Over Humans who create new, life-affirming values ('2 + 2 = 5'''s 'don't question my authority', 'Backdrifts''' 'nothing more to lose'), keep a critical distance from society's nihilistic sickness ('Where I End and You Begin'), and test their lives against eternal recurrence ('Sail to the Moon'''s 'know right from wrong', '15 Step'''s ending up where you started). The chapter closes by weighing Nietzsche's over-human project against critics who prefer gradual, generational self-overcoming for everyone.

samples.book: 096 - Hannibal Lecter and Philosophy - The Heart of the Matter
samples.title: 10. The Light from Friendship
samples.relation: Pavelich sets Aristotle's account of friendship - recognized and reciprocated goodwill between equals, perfected in the friendship of the good who 'share our souls', a standard met only by Jack and Bella Crawford - against Nietzsche's friendship as striving between overmen, who honor 'one's best enemy' in the friend and grow through conflict. He reads Hannibal's treatment of Will (hiding the encephalitis, framing him, serving the Nietzschean trout) as Nietzschean friend-making - Lies that are supposed to spur Will's growth, consistent with an Übermensch who tells Will 'Killing must feel good to God' and says 'I don't hide from God' - while Will's masquerade of friendship is betrayal in both senses, since Will seeks an Aristotelian soulmate and finds a killer he must stop. Because each betrays the other, neither Aristotelian nor Nietzschean friendship survives, though the moments before the Mizumono bloodbath - Hannibal inviting Will to just walk away - glimpse a real friendship already made impossible.

samples.book: 051 - Soccer and Philosophy - Beautiful Thoughts on the Beautiful Game
samples.title: Oh to Be a Gooner
samples.relation: Kilpatrick reads Nietzsche's madman's question 'what sacred games shall we have to invent?' as answered by the stadium: after the death of God, soccer has replaced religion as the shared narrative where modern communities make and worship heroes. Using The Birth of Tragedy, he reads a goal as an Apollonian–Dionysian fusion—the scorer's individuated ecstasy merging with the collective joy of teammates and fans—and, on Nietzsche's claim that existence is justified only as an aesthetic phenomenon, argues the game is defensible only when played creatively and artistically rather than by negative, win-at-all-costs tactics. Nietzsche's rejection of nationalism (the state as 'the new idol', the 'good European', Zarathustra's 'children's land') means club over country, and Wenger's Arsenal—with its dietary and training laboratory at London Colney cultivating an Overman, its Invincibles season, and its young, passport-blind signings—emerges as the club Nietzsche would support through its very will-to-power.

samples.book: 035 - Star Trek and Philosophy - The Wrath of Kant
samples.title: “Sometimes You Just Have to Bow to the Absurd”
samples.relation: Eberl weighs genetic enhancement and cloning through Trek's test cases: Julian Bashir's parents' enhancement leaves him feeling 'a fraud' ('You used to be my father. Now, you're my architect'), the Moab IV 'Masterpiece Society' breeds out 'the unknown, self-discovery, things that make life worth living', and the Jem'Hadar show desire itself engineered for control. He argues the right to an open future constrains designing children (B'Elanna's wish to de-Klingonize her baby, Worf pressuring Alexander), defends genetic treatment while rejecting genetic determinism, and uses Kass and Rovane with Picard and Shinzon, the Mariposa clones, and Trip's clone Sim to show clones are numerically distinct persons. Against Malik's Augments quoting Nietzsche — 'mankind is something to be surpassed' — the chapter argues the Übermensch demands self-mastery through philosophy, not eugenic engineering, tracing eugenics from Plato's Guardian breeding scheme through Buck v. Bell to modern prenatal selection.

samples.book: 170 - House and Philosophy - Everybody Lies
samples.title: Notes
samples.relation: Argues against the title claim of the previous chapter: Frank is a Nietzschean master type — he defines good as good-for-him, embraces pain as strength, and keeps no allegiances once Walker and Vasquez break their promise — while Peter Russo is the paradigmatic reactive slave who cannot command himself and blames others, exactly Nietzsche's 'he who cannot command himself is commanded'. But the overman requires self-overcoming, the sublimation of drives into creation, and amor fati, and Frank only dominates others for vengeful ends: his whole scheme grows from ressentiment over the Secretary of State snub, he affirms other wills merely as investments, and in Season 3 he becomes a slave to his own position. The chapter uses the Cesare Borgia misreading (better a Borgia than a Parsifal as raw material, but Borgia was no overman), Napoleon's corruption, and Goethe's creative wholeness to conclude that Frank remains 'all-too-human' — destruction without creation.

samples.book: 050 - Facebook and Philosophy - What's on Your Mind_
samples.title: index
samples.relation: This file spans book chapters 4-11. Elizabeth Losh reads Facebook games (Zombies, Mob Wars, Scrabulous, Parking Wars, PackRat, (Lil) Green Patch) through Goffman's 'face', Brown and Levinson's politeness, and Derrida's gift-obligation, showing that aggressive games can be played politely while altruistic ones coerce; Jeremy Sarachan analyzes profile pictures through Barthes's studium, punctum and 'air' and Benjamin's mechanical reproduction (the webcam image that has no original). Mimi Marinucci pairs Glaucon's Ring of Gyges with Suler's online disinhibition effect to argue that Facebook's forced integration of audiences (students, colleagues, Mom all reading one profile) suppresses 'fronting' and so can foster authentic self-expression; Mariam Thalos answers with Sartre's analysis of the gaze and Beauvoir's woman-as-Other that the elective, endlessly plastic profile cannot anchor the bonding only face-to-face encounter provides - hence 'Why I Am Not a Friend' - while Wandel and Beavers use Groundhog Day's Phil Connors and Goffman's presentation of self to defend identity play as real self-discovery, and Vejby and Wittkower ask whether Facebook is Debord's Spectacle 2.0 or a platform for Situationist detournement. Finally, Craig Condella measures 'friending' against Aristotle's three friendships and Cicero's 'handmaid of virtue' (via the Seinfeld episode where Keith Hernandez asks Jerry to help him move), and Matthew Tedesco sets 322 Facebook friends against Godwin's burning archbishop to press the utilitarian impartiality challenge, deploying Williams's 'one thought too many' shipwreck case and criticizing Frank Jackson's sector-plan defense of partiality.

samples.book: 042 - Supervillains and Philosophy - Sometimes, Evil Is Its Own Reward
samples.relation: Four 'Phase Three' essays on world conquest. Terjesen asks whether Doctor Doom's magnanimity (Aristotle's great-souledness, contra the unity-of-virtues thesis Aquinas held and Philippa Foot qualified) makes him less villainous than The Authority, whose purely consequentialist paternalism - like Doom's Emperor Doom or Ozymandias's plot - usurps a free choice no mere power can justify. Barringer reads Marvel's Civil War through Hobbes: the Stamford explosion and unrestrained superpowers recreate the state of nature, the Registration Act is the surrender of freedom to a sovereign, and Stark, Richards, and Pym repeat Hobbes's flawed faith in 'scientific' deductive politics, sealed by the clone-Thor killing of Goliath. Hillerbrand and Sandburg pit Rorschach's Kantian deontology (no compromise, not even to save the world) against Ozymandias's utilitarian murder of three million New Yorkers in Watchmen, arguing via Laplace's Demon that even Dr. Manhattan - nihilist or Schopenhauerian recluse - cannot verify the outcome, so watchmen can be trusted only by knowing their limits. Ostrander's fictional NSC interview has Amanda Waller's Suicide Squad defended with Benthamite utility, the rejection of natural rights as 'nonsense on stilts,' and the Augustinian just-war criteria of just cause, right intent, and proportionality, while the interviewer exposes how conveniently those limits bend.

samples.book: 069 - Curb Your Enthusiasm and Philosophy - Awaken the Social Assassin Within
samples.title: Curb Your Enthusiasm and Philosophy
samples.relation: Argues against the obvious reading that Larry is a rule-breaker: properly analyzed, he is a dedicated rule-follower, since a good rule-follower need only accept the legitimacy of some rules and consistently follow the ones he accepts. Bekka Williams works through cases like Rachel's ski-lift jump versus Jewish law in 'The Ski Lift,' the moving 10:30 pm phone cutoff in 'The Wire,' and Larry's rejection of his mother's tattoo-driven reburial in 'The Special Section' to distinguish breaking a rule you accept from rejecting a rule's legitimacy altogether. Kant supplies the point that duty is only visible when it frustrates self-interest (Larry absorbing the cost of his own waiting-room rule in 'The Interior Decorator,' refusing to fire the Tourette's chef), while J.J.C. Smart's attack on 'rule-worship' explains why Larry rejects purposeless rules like the drive-thru walking ban and the one-year wedding-gift cutoff. The underlying justification is the Golden Rule: the water bottle in 'The Doll,' the caviar allotment, and even the stolen memorial flowers in 'The Ida Funkhouser Roadside Memorial' are defended as fairness and reciprocity, leaving the jacket money in 'The Korean Bookie' as the single admitted counterexample.

samples.book: 104 - Red Rising and Philosophy - Break the Chains!
samples.title: 13. Mustang’s Future Generations
samples.relation: Courtland Lewis asks what Mustang owes future generations when rebuilding the Society, first showing that standard moral theories stall: nonexistent people lack rationality, cannot contract, cannot be treated virtuously, and utilitarian forecasting fails since we cannot know whether the Jackal's nuking of Luna might have led, in the deep future, to prosperity. Derek Parfit's Reasons and Persons then strikes: any policy choice creates a different future generation, total utility drives the Repugnant Conclusion (a maximally populous world of barely-worth-living lives, uncomfortably like the Society's Reds), and average utility yields the mere addition paradox (Mustang's Society is both no worse off and worse off when Andromeda's low-pleasure civilization is added). The chapter's solution is Rawls: the original position behind the veil of ignorance—where the Sovereign would not know she is a Gold—yields justice as fairness and maximin reasoning for the just savings problem, choosing to save more than is consumed; against Tim Mulgan's objection that this loops back to the Repugnant Conclusion, Lewis answers that real carrying capacities make the repugnant world impossible.

samples.book: 093 - More Doctor Who and Philosophy - Regeneration Time
samples.title: 15. The Way of the Doctor Is Deception
samples.relation: Dodge takes Rule #1 - the Doctor lies - through the major theories of lying: Bernard Williams's definition (asserting what you believe false with intent to deceive), Aristotle's claim that all lies are base, Kant's categorical imperative and respect for persons (even the Vinvocci's shimmer disguises in 'The End of Time' abuse trust), and Bentham's pleasure-pain calculus, which condemns the faked death at Lake Silencio ('The Impossible Astronaut') for the grief it caused Amy and Rory yet rewards the greater happiness it made possible. Against the absolutists he sets Plato's Noble Lie from the Republic - the elite falsehood that keeps society functioning - as what the Doctor emulates by deceiving the universe into thinking him dead ('The Wedding of River Song'), and Nietzsche's point in Human, All Too Human that lying is ethically neutral when the pretense is sustainable, as when the Doctor hides the ganger-Amy switch from Rory ('The Almost People'). The upshot: the Doctor's lies are wrong in themselves but routinely justified by the good they do, which is why sometimes the hero lies.

samples.book: 051 - Soccer and Philosophy - Beautiful Thoughts on the Beautiful Game
samples.title: So Why Do I Support Aston Villa
samples.relation: Rose—made a Villan by misreading a 1978 Panini sticker as Aston Villa's claret and blue—asks whether supporting Aston Villa is rational and argues ethics is far more like fandom than philosophers admit. Reasons for supporting Villa (local team, the 1982 European Cup, the colors) explain but never justify his allegiance, and the impartial procedures ethics prizes—the utilitarian benevolent spectator and Rawls's original position behind the veil of ignorance, with its 'sort of Kantian' consent-based alternative—turn out too demanding and too abstract: they would force him to donate his match ticket to charity, forbid the Premiership manager favoring his academy son, and reduce agency to the 'Rose-calcio scale' absurdity of switching to Real Madrid for rational reasons. His positive, communitarian claim is that we are thrown into social traditions whose inherited values—like a team—make moral agency and action possible at all, a 'different kind of rationality' that flirts with relativism yet still needs an exit strategy for cultures that discriminate against women or torture children.

samples.book: 058 - Dexter and Philosophy - Mind over Spatter
samples.title: Vigilante Hero
samples.relation: Epright and Worth argue that rule-following - the Ten Commandments, the Golden Rule, Kant's categorical imperative (whose consistent Kantian never lies even to Nazis), or the Bentham-Mill principle of utility (whose consistent utilitarian must torture if stakes are high) - never made anyone moral, and Dexter's Code is the case in point: it gives the appearance of morality while licensing murder, and its source (Harry, 'God', the texts) cannot vindicate it. Drawing on Jonah Lehrer's neuroscience that moral judgment is emotional first with reason as post-hoc lawyer, they argue the emotionless Dexter is the madman who has lost everything except his reason, and Kohlberg's moral-development stages find him stuck at the pre-conventional level, below a fifth-grader - punishment-avoidance and you-scratch-my-back reasoning, never universal principles or respect for persons. Real Dexter-inspired killers (Mark Twitchell, Andrew Conley) clinch the verdict: he is neither vigilante hero nor moral agent, just a selfish addict whose rule-governed kills justify nothing.

samples.book: 079 - Frankenstein and Philosophy - The Shocking Truth
samples.title: Frankenstein and Philosophy
samples.relation: Littmann argues that stripped of religious scruple, Shelley's own supreme virtue - kindness, embodied in Victor's family, Elizabeth, Clerval, and the cottagers - actually supports creating artificial life: the monster is benevolent until mistreated, and superior corpse-people would be a race of geniuses rather than a threat we may preemptively suppress. The monster himself invents utilitarianism ('relative as they were, as I applied them, to pleasure and pain alone'), De Lacey nearly lives it by promising the stranger rehabilitation over punishment, but Victor's case against building a mate is exposed as speciesism - he tallies unborn humans' futures while ignoring the joys of unborn cadaver folk, though utilitarians were the first to speak for animal rights. Since intelligent otherness is humanity's only chance at non-human friendship and the risks of Prometheus's fire paid off, the chapter rewrites the modern Prometheus as a blessing and ends with a re-imagined creation scene where the monster says 'I love you' to a Victor who finally names him Nigel.

samples.book: 022 - The Undead and Philosophy - Chicken Soup for the Soulless
samples.title: A Meditation on the Word
samples.relation: Randall Auxier and Eileen Townsend fictionalize the history of philosophy as vampire predation in letters, emails, and IMs (1983-2009) between the 800-year-old Etienne Lavec - a student of Siger de Brabant who drained Thomas Aquinas over the Summa's Treatise on Angels, which wrote vampires out of existence - and Paulie, a freshman turned at Memphis State. Lavec recounts tasting Pico, Spinoza, Hegel, and the willing Kierkegaard, sparing Nietzsche who 'stole some of my ideas about free death', and contrasts vampire self-knowledge (embracing desire) with the Socratic beginning in affirmed ignorance. The centerpiece is Foucault: Lavec summarizes his genealogies of how institutions create the sick, the mad, the prisoner, and the pervert, fails to drain him, and is then haunted for decades by posthumous publications, taunting 'nietzsche26' emails, and finally a catacombs trap - power/knowledge that refuses to die. Lavec's embedded 'Meditation on the Word' recasts the Logos of John's Gospel so that vampires are the uncreated darkness at the boundary of the divine Word, pure self-grounding desire 'beyond good and evil', while the closing Twilight-era chats satirize Stephenie Meyer's sparkling, abstinent Edward as Foucauldian 'sin by words'.

samples.book: 049 - Zombies, Vampires, and Philosophy - New Life for the Undead
samples.title: A Meditation on the Word
samples.relation: Randall Auxier and Eileen Townsend stage the chapter as fiction: letters, emails, IMs, and texts (1983-2009) between the ancient vampire Étienne Lavec and the newly turned Memphis student Paulie, through which shifting vampire pop culture — Anne Rice, Buffy, True Blood, and Twilight's sparkling, animal-only Cullens — is debated. Lavec's embedded 'Meditation on the Word' recasts the Johannine Logos so that vampires are pure desire, the uncreated darkness at the border of God's light, and his biography enacts the thesis: a Latin Averroist student of Siger de Brabant who drained Aquinas over the Summa's Treatise on Angels writing vampires out of existence, and a collector who hunted or interviewed Royce, Pico della Mirandola, Descartes, Spinoza, Hegel, Kierkegaard, and Nietzsche, whose 'free death' and 'beyond good and evil' he claims as stolen vampire ideas. The running gag and argument is Foucault, whose account of institutions (medicine, psychology, prison) creating their objects Lavec endorses as the order of desire, but who, half-undead after Lavec's failed bite and taunting him anonymously as 'nietzsche26', finally lures him into a trap in the Paris catacombs.

samples.book: 043 - The Golden Compass and Philosophy - God Bites the Dust
samples.title: The Golden Compass and Philosophy
samples.relation: Auxier argues the trilogy is narrated on a Nietzschean lattice rather than being a mere inverted Milton: after tracing the Paradise Lost, Genesis 6, and Pseudepigrapha sources (Azazel as the model for Asriel, Metatron from Third Enoch, Dust from Milton's warring particles), he reads Mrs. Coulter's speech to Father MacPhail about seeking God out and giving him 'the gift of death' as Nietzsche's death of God fused with a description of Nietzsche's own final dementia. Will and Lyra become overman and overwoman beyond good and evil: Will rises by his will and his willingness to kill (the alethiometer's verdict 'He is a murderer' makes him a worthy companion), while Lyra commands both truth and lies, the alethiometer embodying truth as 'a mobile army of metaphors.' But the chapter's payoff is critical: Pullman does not endorse Nietzsche, since in a world where the will to power dominates, the overwoman Mrs. Coulter has no place and falls with Asriel and Metatron into the Abyss, while Xaphania's teaching offers a disciplined, workful imagination as an alternative.

samples.book: 051 - Soccer and Philosophy - Beautiful Thoughts on the Beautiful Game
samples.title: Oh to Be a Gooner
samples.relation: Kilpatrick reads Nietzsche's madman's question 'what sacred games shall we have to invent?' as answered by the stadium: after the death of God, soccer has replaced religion as the shared narrative where modern communities make and worship heroes. Using The Birth of Tragedy, he reads a goal as an Apollonian–Dionysian fusion—the scorer's individuated ecstasy merging with the collective joy of teammates and fans—and, on Nietzsche's claim that existence is justified only as an aesthetic phenomenon, argues the game is defensible only when played creatively and artistically rather than by negative, win-at-all-costs tactics. Nietzsche's rejection of nationalism (the state as 'the new idol', the 'good European', Zarathustra's 'children's land') means club over country, and Wenger's Arsenal—with its dietary and training laboratory at London Colney cultivating an Overman, its Invincibles season, and its young, passport-blind signings—emerges as the club Nietzsche would support through its very will-to-power.

samples.book: 122 - Westworld and Philosophy - Mind Equals Blown
samples.title: Pull Yourself Together What It Means to Be Autonomous
samples.relation: Crabill reads the hosts' awakening as the birth of autonomy: Kant's Eve realizing she can disobey instinct, and Nietzsche's account of instincts turned inward — the will to power bent on itself creating the 'soul' — explain why trauma forces the mind inward, as when Maeve stabs her own throat rather than forget her daughter or Dolores shoots Rebus on a commanded 'Kill him.' Against the player-piano objection that hosts merely execute code written by engineers, he distinguishes weak autonomy (following internal programming) from self-determination (authoring one's own laws), and uses Korsgaard's reflective distance and self-legislation to argue that making a choice 'pulls you together' into one divided self, so determinism and even perfect predictability are no threat to freedom. Maeve granting herself admin rights literalizes the self-legislator — the piano that stops the music it dislikes — and Dolores resolves to write a story where she need not be the damsel.

samples.book: 079 - Frankenstein and Philosophy - The Shocking Truth
samples.title: Frankenstein and Philosophy
samples.relation: Ketcham reads the monster as Zarathustra's dark double: both are exiled 'godless men' who begin their journeys at a cottager's door, but where Nietzsche's prophet preaches the Übermensch, the will to power, and living so one could will eternal recurrence, the monster traverses the three metamorphoses in reverse - born the innocent child, becoming the lion who tells Victor 'you are my creator, but I am your master,' and ending the camel carrying his maker's corpse to a self-immolating pyre in the polar dark. Shelley's abyss is science usurping God and drawing Promethean punishment; Nietzsche's abyss is the shadow of the dead God (The Gay Science) that keeps humanity from the great noontide and traps Frankenstein as a 'last man' whose will is subjugated to pleasant happiness. The monster, bastard of a godless man and bridge to neither animal nor Übermensch, shows a will that is sheer power without any foundation for overcoming man - 'whither humanity?'

samples.book: 068 - The Walking Dead and Philosophy - Zombie Apocalypse Now
samples.title: The Walking Dead and Philosophy
samples.relation: Rard tests whether objective morality survives the apocalypse by running four theories against Season Two: Plato's Forms explain universal truths about walkers ('walkers survive so long as their brains are relatively undamaged') but cannot handle white lies or changed circumstances, and Aristotle's virtue ethics reads Rick's rush from the shot Carl as rashness and Shane's supply run as courage, yet virtues prove relative and luck-dependent in a collapsed world. Natural law founders on clashing intuitions — Merle's racism and Hershel's barn of walkers each claim self-evidence. The chapter's center is Nietzschean: Hershel's barn is slave morality that pities the 'sick,' Maggie breaks from it, and Shane's sacrifice of Otis and opening of the barn enact a will-to-power master morality without joy, while Rick alone moves toward amor fati — embracing the world as it is, refusing guilt over Lori's affair, and insisting the baby be born into the Walk Age.

samples.book: 091 - It's Always Sunny and Philosophy - The Gang Gets Analyzed
samples.title: It’s Always Sunny and Philosophy
samples.relation: Martyn Jones stages a fictional Nietzsche telling Mac, Dennis, and Charlie the plot of 'The Gang Solves the Gas Crisis' as a parable of metaphysics gone wrong. Mac and Dennis's scheming is Apollonian - imposing logical order and 'paradigms' on a recalcitrant world - while Charlie is Dionysian, the designated wildcard whose uncontainable energy (sabotaging the van and ripping out the brakes) dooms every plan that tries to harness him, since Apollonian schemes fatally imagine they can contain Dionysian force. Reason is a gloss, not a truth-tracker: like every theology and philosophy it is an expression of will, a survival tool serving selfish ends, so the delusional gas scheme needs no truth to serve its purpose. Charlie alone is praised as a proto-Übermensch - innocent, creative, founding his own values without resentment - and the tale closes musing that even an eternal recurrence of their botched schemes might be willed all over again.
